FUNCTIONAL GENOMICS · PLANT–MICROBE–SOIL INTERACTIONS

From molecules to living systems:
Discovery rooted in biology.

The Solanki Lab is based in the Department of Agronomy, Horticulture and Plant Science at South Dakota State University. Our research integrates multiple approaches to explore how plants, microbes, and soil interact—and how understanding these relationships can help us develop more resilient crops.

Explore our research ↗

01 / RESEARCH

Small interactions.
Far-reaching questions.

FG–PMSI
01 / IMMUNITY

Plant Immunity

Investigating the molecular mechanisms that shape how plants recognize and respond to pathogens.

Explore the theme ↗02 / MICROBIOME

Microbial Solutions

Discovering soil microbial communities and beneficial microorganisms that support plant health, disease suppression, and crop resilience.

Explore the theme ↗03 / GENOMICS

Functional Genomics

Connecting genes, expression, and biological function to understand complex plant–microbe–soil relationships.

Explore the theme ↗04 / PROTEIN DESIGN

AI–Protein Modeling

AI-guided modeling and design of NLR immune receptor function for temperature adaptation and disease resistance.

Explore the theme ↗05 / CROP HEALTH

Resilient Crops

Bringing molecular insight into disease resistance to develop practical crop health solutions.

02 / OUR APPROACH

Lab-to-Land Approach

Molecular discovery, guided by the needs of agriculture.

01

Genome Sequencing

Read the biological blueprint.

Sequence plant, pathogen, and microbial genomes to characterize diversity and identify candidate genes and biological functions.

02

Spatial Transcriptomics

Locate the response.

Connect gene expression with tissue structure to understand where and when resistance responses unfold.

03

Genetic Engineering

Test the mechanism.

Use molecular tools to test gene function and evaluate approaches to plant immunity and microbial crop protection.

04

Stakeholder Input

Start with field priorities.

Work with farmers and industry partners to connect research questions with disease pressure, crop health, and production needs.

05

Institutional / Collaborative Integration

Bring the expertise together.

Combine expertise across institutions and disciplines to connect molecular discovery, validation, formulation, and agricultural application.

Functional Genomics → Plant–Microbe–Soil Interactions → Molecular Discovery → Translation → Crop Resilience

03 / ABOUT THE TEAM

Team-enabled science

Our laboratory brings together people working across molecular biology, genomics, imaging, computational analysis, and field research.

Meet the team ↗

04 / OUTREACH

Science in the community.

Hands-on genomics education, conversations in the field, and local industry partnerships connect our laboratory with the people it serves.
